vulnerabilities.description: A buffer overflow in SQLite source snapshots/builds containing Fossil check-in 8bdc0d485e3ad0c7a1e818da66f106951d496b05cbe61d12c2c448f2f24b6d5d and later snapshots/builds can cause denial of service via the ext/misc/sqlar.c sqlarUncompressFunc()/sqlar_uncompress() code path.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not invoke the affected SQLite snapshot-only sqlar decompression path.

ratings.justification: Exploitation requires the specific SQLite sqlar snapshot code path, and no such API usage exists in the stock Liquibase Secure runtime.

analysis.detail: This SQLite issue is limited to snapshot builds containing the sqlarUncompressFunc/sqlar_uncompress code path in ext/misc/sqlar.c. The Liquibase Secure image inherits the OS package from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (`docker/Dockerfile:2`) and the container entrypoint execs only the Liquibase CLI (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8`, `docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119`). A focused grep across the runtime Dockerfiles, entrypoint scripts, and application source found no references to sqlarUncompressFunc, sqlar_uncompress, sqlite3_value_int64, or sqlite3_malloc, so the vulnerable snapshot-only code path is not reachable from the stock runtime.
